classification.difficultyReason: Simplify the logarithms to zero and carry the original domain through to a ray with an excluded endpoint.

answer.short: $y=0$ for $x>0$, with an open circle at $(0,0)$.
answer.worked:
The original logarithms require $x>0$. On this domain, use the product law.
$$\begin{align*}
y&=\ln(x)+\ln\!\left(\frac1x\right)\\
y&=\ln\!\left(x\cdot\frac1x\right)\\
y&=\ln 1\\
y&=0
\end{align*}$$
Draw the ray along the positive $x$-axis with an open circle at the origin because $x=0$ is outside the domain.

spec.sourceRegion: Answer book, printed page 365, right column P6
spec.description: Blue rightward ray on black axes with a blue open circle at the origin and the original domain caption below the ray.
spec.mathematics: y=0 exactly when x is in the domain x>0. The origin is excluded.
